summary: Verified fixes for (1) duplicate orders race and (2) UTC timezone normalisation on Cravitoo. Backend pytest and Playwright UI tests for both employee and vendor Orders pages all pass with the pre-seeded TIMEFIX orders.

details: GET /api/orders (employee): returns exactly 2 orders CRV-TIMEFIX1 and CRV-TIMEFIX2, unique ids, created_at values end with '+00:00' (2026-06-15T04:00:00+00:00 and 2026-06-15T13:45:00+00:00).
GET /api/orders (vendor): returns the same 2 orders, unique collection codes, created_at UTC-aware.

frontend_playwright.employee_orders_page: Rendered EXACTLY 2 order cards - CRV-TIMEFIX1 (15 June 2026 at 04:00 am) and CRV-TIMEFIX2 (15 June 2026 at 01:45 pm). No duplicates. No 'Invalid Date' string on page.
frontend_playwright.vendor_orders_page: Rendered EXACTLY 2 order cards - CRV-TIMEFIX1 (6/15/2026, 4:00:00 AM) and CRV-TIMEFIX2 (6/15/2026, 1:45:00 PM). No duplicates. No 'Invalid Date' string on page.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct: atomic find_one_and_update on {cravitoo_order_id: None} with __materialising__ sentinel plus poll-wait for losing caller eliminates the /verify vs webhook race.
GET /api/orders normalises created_at to UTC-aware ISO string (ends with +00:00); browser Date parsing then renders correct local time.
seed_data_creation: Used pre-seeded orders CRV-TIMEFIX1 and CRV-TIMEFIX2; did not create new data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Razorpay is in LIVE mode (RAZORPAY_MOCK_MODE=false) - do NOT attempt live checkout via UI. Duplicate-order race deterministic test is /app/backend/scripts/test_duplicate_order_race.py. New regression test at /app/backend/tests/test_timefix_orders.py covers the duplicate + UTC created_at fix.
rca of the issue: Duplicate orders were caused by Razorpay /verify endpoint and the async Razorpay webhook both calling _finalize_payment_intent concurrently; each inserted its own order document. Fix: atomically claim the intent via find_one_and_update setting cravitoo_order_id='__materialising__' only when previously None; the winner materialises the order, the loser polls until the real order id appears and returns it. Time inaccuracy was caused by created_at stored/returned as naive datetime; browser assumed local timezone. Fix: GET /api/orders coerces created_at to timezone-aware UTC and serialises as ISO string with '+00:00' suffix so the browser converts to correct local time.
